competitors.name: Publix / GreenWise
competitors.action: Supermarket News reported that Publix and distributor Quirch Foods face a wrongful-death and personal-injury lawsuit alleging that recalled GreenWise Organic frozen blueberries caused one consumer's death and another consumer's hospitalization. The underlying E. coli O145:H28 outbreak is over, according to the CDC; health departments reported 17 confirmed illnesses and six hospitalizations, while the CDC said it received no attributable deaths among confirmed cases.

trends.topic: Frozen private-label recalls escalating into retailer and distributor liability claims
trends.magnitude: The GreenWise frozen-fruit incident progressed from a July recall to a September lawsuit naming both Publix and Quirch Foods; the CDC's final count was 17 confirmed illnesses and six hospitalizations.
trends.context: The alleged death has not been attributed to the outbreak by public-health agencies, so the lawsuit remains a claim rather than a confirmed causal finding. Even so, the escalation shows that frozen suppliers, distributors and retailer-owned brands can remain exposed after an outbreak closes, strengthening the case for lot-level traceability, documented quality controls and rapid recall execution.

breaking.headline: Publix sued over alleged E. coli death
